newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa platinum shares rush on metal price rally.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa platinum shares rush on metal price rally.

text.p: A richer platinum price fuelled South African platinum shares in early Thursday trade with stocks in the recently strike-hit Rustenburg mine rushing more than six percent higher.

Dealers said the overnight rally in the metal price -- last fixed at $417.50 an ounce, its highest since February 21, 1996 -- was causing the hunger for the stocks but they questioned how long the sudden surge could last.
"They must be climbing on the back of that (platinum price) news. Platinum jumped very sharply overnight," said Johan Marais, dealer at Societe Geneneral Frankel Pollak.
"The question you have to ask is how long can this price rise last. It's been firming since the strike news," he added.
Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd rushed up 425 cents to 74.50 rand as investors took heart from the metal price and further encouragement from the strike's halt.

But dealers said the market was a little puzzled as to why the platinum price, fuelled on Wednesday by the wildcat work stoppage at Rustenburg, the world's biggest producer, suddenly took off when the strike ended.
"You'd think that after it was concentrated on for so long, the end of the Rusplats strike would cap prices," a dealer said.
The strike by 4,600 workers began on Monday night and workers returned to work on Thursday night. Mine managers Anglo American Platinum Corp said limited output was lost.
London traders said the strike helped bolster the platinum price but continuing tight nearby supplies due to a lack of Russian shipments and general covering was driving prices.

Amplats shares added 125 cents to 31.75 rand, Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd jumped 90 cents to 28.80 rand and Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd gained 10 cents to 300 cents. Impala Platinum Holdings also climbed 150 cents to 46 rand.
